the_day: Anthropic previewed its Claude Duet agent, Meta reported quarterly results and a new class of non-voting shares, an outside evaluator found weaknesses in OpenAI's agent monitoring, and xAI launched a partner network for Grok.

items.headline: Anthropic previews Claude Duet, an agent that acts without being asked
points: Anthropic announced a research preview of Claude Duet, a personal AI agent that takes actions on its own, Reuters and CNBC report.
VentureBeat says it works on mobile and desktop. PYMNTS reports it can buy business supplies for users.
Gizmodo says most people probably cannot try it yet.
items.for_you: Claude Duet is a separate agent app in research preview, and access appears to be limited for now.

points: CyberSecurityNews reports Claude Security now scans repositories continuously to find vulnerabilities and track whether they get fixed.

Neither source is an Anthropic post describing the feature.

items.headline: Reservoir sues Anthropic and Suno over songs used by AI
points: Music company Reservoir has filed copyright lawsuits against Anthropic and Suno, Billboard and Music Business Worldwide report.
Music Business Worldwide says the claims cover songs by Joni Mitchell, Johnny Cash, Madonna and others.
In a separate existing case, Reuters reports Anthropic and music publishers argued over Anthropic's fair use defense.

items.headline: Former Harvard AI adviser joins the trust that oversees Anthropic
points: The Harvard Crimson reports that a former Harvard AI adviser has joined Anthropic's oversight trust, weeks after leaving his Harvard role.
Fortune reported yesterday that the new member is astrophysicist Chris Stubbs and that the trust controls Anthropic's board.

items.headline: Google DeepMind publishes a global map of forest types
points: Google DeepMind released a global map that sorts every 10-meter patch of land on Earth into different forest types.
Google describes the map as going beyond measuring tree cover alone.

items.headline: Meta reports quarterly results and creates shares without voting rights
points: Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion and took a $9.89 billion legal charge, Techloy reports.
Several outlets report that Meta is creating a new class of shares without voting rights through a 2-for-1 stock split.
Meta says Muse passed 10 million US downloads in 40 days and that Meta AI use per person has more than doubled since April.
